When deciding whether to combat a fire, all three of these questions are critical safety considerations:

A. "Am I safe from toxic smoke and gases?" - This is essential because toxic smoke and gases can be immediately life-threatening, sometimes more dangerous than the fire itself.

B. "Do I have an escape route?" - This is crucial because if the fire grows or changes direction, you need to be able to evacuate safely.

C. "Do I have the right extinguisher?" - This is important because using the wrong type of extinguisher can be ineffective or even dangerous (e.g., using water on an electrical fire).

In fire safety training, people are typically taught to assess their own safety first, ensure they have an escape route, and then determine if they have the appropriate equipment before attempting to fight a fire. All three of these considerations are part of standard fire safety protocols.
